cards.title: Shopify backend launch order
cards.summary: Sequence the pre-launch Shopify backend tasks in the order that prevents rework: general settings, payments, shipping, policies, domain, then remove the storefront password.
cards.use_when: Preparing a newly built Shopify store to go live (final backend pass before publishing).
steps: In Settings > General, confirm store name, billing address, currency and default units. Getting these wrong affects order records later.

Settings > Payments: activate Shopify Payments and connect the bank account. Have an ID document (driver's licence or passport) ready — identity verification is part of activation. Optionally add extra methods (e.g. crypto) via Add payment method; availability varies by region.
Settings > Shipping and delivery: define zones and rates (details in the shipping card).
Settings > Policies: generate refund, privacy, terms and contact templates; write a custom shipping policy (no template).
Settings > Domains: connect an existing domain or buy one (the tutorial quotes roughly $16/year; verify current pricing).
Online store: click Remove password — the store is inaccessible to customers until this is done.
caveats: The presenter skips Shopify's onboarding questionnaire, noting it does not change what you get in the backend; skipping is fine but you must supply business details from your own records.
Domain pricing and payment-method availability change over time — verify the current Shopify interface.
Tax setup is jurisdiction-specific; consult a tax professional.
cards.source_name: Shopify Tutorial for Beginners 2026 - Full Store Setup Guide.docx

cards.title: Adding product variants for size and colour
cards.summary: Use Shopify's variant section to sell size/colour combinations, setting per-variant prices where larger sizes or colours should cost more.
cards.use_when: Product setup for an apparel store where one listing must cover multiple sizes or colours.
steps: Open the variant section while editing a product and add options such as size and colour.
Add each option value so Shopify creates the variant grid.

Set a distinct price per variant where justified (e.g. larger sizes or premium colours). In the tutorial's example the base product is $49 and variants are left at the default, but Shopify supports different prices per variant.
Check inventory per variant after saving so each size/colour tracks separately.
Save and confirm the variants appear on the product page and are selectable.
caveats: Variant-level pricing is supported but the tutorial does not test it here; verify on your own listing.
Skipping variants entirely means one price and one stock count for the whole product.
cards.source_name: Shopify Tutorial for Beginners 2026 - Full Store Setup Guide.docx

cards.title: Compare-at price strike-through
cards.summary: Enter a higher 'compare at' price so the product page shows the current price as a discount off a struck-through original.
cards.use_when: Pricing a product on its Shopify product page when you want visible discount framing.
steps: While editing a product, set the Price field to the actual selling price (e.g. $49 in the tutorial).
Fill the Compare at price field with the higher reference price. Shopify renders it as a strikethrough next to the live price.
Save and preview the product page to check the discount reads clearly and the reference price is credible.
caveats: The source presents this purely as a visual discount effect; it does not validate the fairness or legality of the reference price.
Displaying a permanently raised compare-at price undermines trust if customers see the 'discount' never ends.

cards.title: Inventory tracking and out-of-stock behaviour
cards.summary: Decide whether an item shows 'sold out' or keeps selling when inventory hits zero, based on whether you can actually restock on demand.
cards.use_when: Backend inventory setup for a store deciding how to handle a product running out.
steps: Under Inventory, enter the current stock count; Shopify decrements it automatically on each sale.
Leave 'continue selling when out of stock' off if you want the storefront to show a sold-out state when the count reaches zero.
Turn it on if the product can be sourced after the sale (e.g. dropshipping) so checkout is not blocked.
When new stock arrives, manually update the count.
If you enable continued selling, watch that you can genuinely fulfil those orders or your refund/dispute rate will suffer.
caveats: The source frames this as 'up to you' with no single rule; it notes manually adjusting the number when restocking.
cards.source_name: Shopify Tutorial for Beginners 2026 - Full Store Setup Guide.docx

cards.title: Manual collections: build category pages from a product list
cards.summary: Create manual collections so the storefront can show category pages (e.g. Shirts) and home-page grids built from hand-picked products.
cards.use_when: Organising products into shoppable categories for navigation and the home page.
steps: Go to Products > Collections and add a collection.
Give it a clear category title and upload a collection image — the image appears in collection lists and grids.
Keep the collection type as Manual so you control membership.
Under Products, click Browse, select the products for this collection and add them, then Save.
Repeat for each category and for any curated set (the tutorial also builds a 'New arrivals' collection for home-page featuring).
If Shopify pre-creates collections you do not want (e.g. a default Home page collection), delete it to keep the list clean.
caveats: Manual collections do not auto-update as new products are added — you maintain them by hand, so revisit them when you add products.
Collection images interact with the storefront layout (grids and lists) so choose crops that read at thumbnail size.
cards.source_name: Shopify Tutorial for Beginners 2026 - Full Store Setup Guide.docx

cards.title: Delete default shipping zones before adding your own
cards.summary: Remove Shopify's default weight-based US zone and rates, then build your own zone and flat rates so pricing reflects your actual fulfilment.
cards.use_when: Shipping configuration on a new store where default rates do not match your shipping plan.
steps: Settings > Shipping and delivery shows a profile for all products (one profile is fine for a simple store).
Inspect the default zone: domestic shipping with weight-based rates and a free-shipping threshold ($50 and up in the tutorial).
Delete the default zone via the three-dot menu > Delete — the source stresses this as a necessary step before adding your own.
Click Add shipping zone, type the region (e.g. US), select it and Click done.
Click Add rate, choose Flat rate (or dynamic rates by weight/volume/carrier), pick the shipping type (Standard, Express, Economy) and set the price — the tutorial uses Standard $6 and Express $15.
Save and confirm the buyer-facing options at checkout.
caveats: The transcript's 'Add rate' menu offers flat, dynamic and carrier-based rates; use flat only if you are not metering weight or volume.
The $6/$15 figures are the source's example prices, not a benchmark — set rates to match your real costs.
cards.source_name: Shopify Tutorial for Beginners 2026 - Full Store Setup Guide.docx

cards.title: Product shipping weight and box volume
cards.summary: Fill shipping weight and volume on products only if you intend to charge weight- or volume-based rates; flat-rate shippers can skip them.
cards.use_when: Product setup where you are deciding whether to populate shipping dimensions.
steps: Under the product's Shipping section, enter the weight of the product and the volume of the box you ship it in.
Use these fields only if your shipping rates are calculated by weight or volume.
If you charge a flat rate, leave them blank — the tutorial deliberately skips them because it uses flat rates.
caveats: Weight/volume only affects pricing if the matching rate type is active in shipping settings; filling fields without a dynamic rate does nothing.
Accurate numbers matter later if you switch to dynamic rates; loose estimates produce wrong charges.
cards.source_name: Shopify Tutorial for Beginners 2026 - Full Store Setup Guide.docx

cards.title: Product description and imagery for the PDP
cards.summary: Write the title and description first, then add high-quality images and choose which one leads on the product page.
cards.use_when: Adding or improving a product listing on a Shopify store.
steps: Enter the product title, then the description; if stuck, use Shopify's built-in AI description helper (source offers this without judging quality).
Drag several high-quality product images in, showing the product in its best light.
Rearrange the image order because the first image is the one customers see on product and collection pages.
Optionally complete the search-engine listing section of the product to control how the item appears in search results (the source leaves it default here).
Save and preview on desktop and mobile.
caveats: The source notes you should use high-quality images but offers no pixel or count guidance; decide based on your product.
AI-written descriptions are offered as a convenience, not vetted for accuracy or brand voice.
